stemMarkdown: The price of an article is first increased by 32%, and then the new price is decreased by 13%. What is the net percentage change in price? (Enter a negative value if it is a net decrease.)
solutionMarkdown: Take the original price as 100. After a 32% increase: $100 \times (1 + 32/100) = 132.00$. After a 13% decrease on 132.00: $132.00 \times (1 - 13/100) = 114.84$. Net change $= 114.84 - 100 = 14.84\%$.
altSolutionMarkdown: Shortcut formula: net \% change $= p_1 - p_2 - \dfrac{p_1 p_2}{100} = 32 - 13 - \dfrac{416}{100} = 14.84\%$.
